name: Newfoundland and Labrador
summary_text: No province-specific trans law, enforcement pattern or official statement was found: criminal law and the federal human-rights framework apply uniformly, and the province has no facility or expression rule differing from the national position. Police-reported hate crime across all motivations is the lowest in the country alongside Manitoba (5.3 per 100,000 in 2024); a +51% rise that year was from very small absolute numbers. Risk assessed at parity with the national picture.

sources.title: The Daily — Police-reported hate crime in Canada, 2024
sources.claim_summary: Statistics Canada's release "Police-reported hate crime in Canada, 2024" (30 Mar 2026): 4,882 hate crimes reported nationally, +1% over 2023 (rate 11.9 per 100,000, -2%); incidents targeting gender identity or expression rose for a fourth consecutive year, +8% to 139 (nearly tripled, +184%, since 2020), and of known specific motivations more than half (56 of 98) targeted intersex, transgender, agender or non-binary people; sexual-orientation-motivated crimes fell 26% to 658 but remain above pre-2023 levels, with June (Pride season) running about twice the monthly average. National series - the release shows no trans-specific provincial pattern for this division. Provincial detail: Newfoundland and Labrador recorded the lowest overall hate-crime rate in the country; its +51% rise (19 incidents in 2023 to 29 in 2024) is attributed to small-number variability, not a trans-specific signal.
